analysis.title: Top Stories (McKeon, Jack) 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Trump arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit and talks with Xi and Putin. Xi greeted him at the airport, which the note calls a rare move. Xi warned against economic barriers, and Putin said sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions cannot hold back rising competitors.
Singapore expects some impact on the flow of high-end chips through the city-state from tighter US curbs. Officials said the fallout can be managed.
Russia imported a record 390,000 tons of petrol by sea in October (Kpler data) after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged refineries and cut production capacity.

After nearly nine months of war, the US and Iran are in a stalemate, each acting as if time is on its side. Former US Middle East negotiators, European officials and Gulf sources say fighting could resume before a diplomatic exit is possible.
Iran struck Kuwait and Bahrain early Wednesday and continued attacks on ships trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

UK CPI rose 3.6% y/y in October, up from 3.5% in September, the highest in a year and a fourth consecutive increase. Energy bills and motor fuel drove it. The print was in line with economists' expectations.
Wall Street banks expect global corporate profit growth to slow sharply next year as the acceleration in AI investment that has supported the equity bull market eases.
Banks that lent billions to finance AI infrastructure are seeking to reduce risk exposure. Scrutiny has increased after the Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections.
Canadian PM Carney will meet Trump at APEC. He reports some progress on a trade deal, 'two steps forward, one step back'.
GS Prime Book data show Fundamental L/S gross leverage down 4.4 pts MTD in November to 206.3% and net leverage down 7.6 pts MTD to 41.6%, a 5-year low for net.
Indonesia's central bank raised its policy rate by 25bp to 6%.
Japan's October imports rose 21.6% y/y against Street +25.9%, and exports rose 20.5% against Street +20.4%.
Today's US calendar includes housing starts, building permits and pending home sales, FOMC minutes at 2:00 pm ET, and remarks from Fed officials Daly, Barr, Williams and Kashkari.
